label: Писать
description: A 10-sentence conjugation card for писать (to write).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person singular present. 'Пишу' shows the с-to-ш consonant mutation typical of писать, with the ending -у. 'Письмо' is the accusative object and 'другу' the dative recipient.
Strategic focus: Second-person singular present. 'Пишешь' keeps the mutated stem пиш- and adds -ешь. 'По-русски' is the adverb of language, describing how you write.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 'Пишет' is the он-form with the -ет ending on the mutated stem. 'Интересную книгу' is the accusative object.
Strategic focus: First-person plural present. 'Пишем' is the мы-form ending in -ем, still on the stem пиш-. 'Писать тест' means to sit or take a written exam.
Strategic focus: Third-person plural present. 'Пишут' closes the present ladder with the -ут ending on пиш-. 'Длинные сочинения' is the plural accusative object.

missions.phrase: Вчера я писал доклад весь вечер.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine past tense. 'Писал' is the masculine singular past of imperfective писать. 'Весь вечер' stresses the ongoing process; the perfective написать would mark completion.
Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 'Писала' adds the feminine -а ending. 'Каждый день' underlines the repeated action that the imperfective conveys.
Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 'Писали' is the plural past ending in -и. 'Диктант' is the accusative object and 'в тетрадях' the prepositional of place.
Strategic focus: Perfective future, first-person. 'Напишу' is the perfective написать with future meaning, promising one completed message. 'Завтра' marks the time and 'тебе' the recipient.
Strategic focus: Singular imperative. 'Пиши' is the informal command formed from the present stem пиш-. It is the everyday way to ask someone to keep in touch.
